newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MILLWALL HAVE DEBTS OF 10 MILLION POUNDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILLWALL HAVE DEBTS OF 10 MILLION POUNDS.

text.p: Millwall Holdings Plc, the parent of London soccer club Millwall, has 10 million pounds ($16.6 million) of debt and is still losing money, the administrator called in to repair the club's finances said.

"The position is bad. There is 10 million pounds of debt and the club is losing around a quarter of a million pounds a month. It is a very difficult situation," David Buchler of Buchler Phillips told a news conference on Wednesday.

Millwall shares were suspended on Tuesday and administrators were called in to run the company while it seeks to put together a financial rescue package. The shares, suspended at four pence, were issued at 20p seven years ago.

The company made a pre-tax loss of 2.9 million pounds in the year to end-May 1996 when the soccer team was relegated to the English second division after a dramatic late slump in form. They are now among the leading clubs in the hunt for promotion.
Buchler said administration meant the club was able to talk meaningfully with its creditor banks. But he admitted the club faced a difficult time.
Peter Mead, chairman of Millwall, said he was confident the club would survive and said he believed it would still be playing into his old age.
"Let me reassure our fans that Millwall will be playing here when my son is wheeling me in and handing me my zimmer frame," Mead told the news conference. ($1=.6035 Pound)
